To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reaction CH3CHCH + O2 is chain branching at high pressures and low temperatures, while the reaction CH3CCH + O2 has a negligible effect on the ignition of propene.
the rate constants for CH3CCHO + O2 and CH3CO + CH2O are chain propagating, and that the rate constants of these reactions have a modest effect in the ignition of propene.

the reaction of CH2CH2 + O2 is chain terminating, but the reaction of CH(CH3) + O2 remains chain propagating at high temperatures, and that the new rate constants for the CH(CH3)CH2 + O 2 reaction have only a small effect on the ignition delays and laminar flame speed of propene.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methylvinyl radical is an important intermediate in the oxidation of propene and its derivatives.
the methyl-vinylethylene + O2 reaction is chain-terminating and the methyl-vinylene + O2 reactions are chain-propagating, even at temperatures up to 2000 K.
the C3H5+O2 reactions are not as important as C2H3+O2 for the oxidation of propene, but the methyl-vinylether (MVK) channel is important in the high-temperature region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C3H5 + O2 reaction does not play a significant role in the combustion of propene.
the reaction of methyl-vinyl and molecular oxygen is a chain propagating reaction, and thus it should be included in combustion models.
the methyl-vinylene radical is an important intermediate in low temperature oxidation chemistry.
